questions.text:
The country of Zombieland is in distress since more than 75% of its working population is suffering from serious health issues. Studies conducted by competent health experts concluded that a complete lack of physical exercise among its working population was one of the leading causes of their health issues. As one of the measures to address the problem, the Government of Zombieland has decided to provide monetary incentives to those who ride bicycles to work.

Based only on the information provided above, which one of the following statements can be logically inferred with certainty?

options.A: All the working population of Zombieland will henceforth ride bicycles to work.
options.B: Riding bicycles will ensure that all of the working population of Zombieland is free of health issues.
options.C: The health experts suggested to the Government of Zombieland to declare riding bicycles as mandatory.
options.D: The Government of Zombieland believes that riding bicycles is a form of physical exercise.

questions.text:
Consider the following C code and corresponding assembly code. Operands U1–U4 are unknown. Registers r1–r5 are 32-bit integer registers; initially r1 = 0, r2 = 10, and r3 and r4 contain the base addresses of arrays a and b. Memory is byte-addressable.

C code:
```c
int a[10], b[10], i;
for (i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    a[i] = b[i] * 8;
}
```

Assembly code:
```asm
L01: jeq r1, r2, end  ; if (r1 == r2) goto end
L02: lw  r5, 0(r4)    ; r5 <- Memory[r4+0]
L03: shl r5, r5, U1   ; r5 <- r5 << U1
L04: sw  r5, 0(r3)    ; Memory[r3+0] <- r5
L05: add r3, r3, U2   ; r3 <- r3 + U2
L06: add r4, r4, U3
L07: add r1, r1, 1
L08: jmp U4           ; goto U4
L09: end
```

Which option correctly replaces (U1, U2, U3, U4) in the assembly code?

Let U = {1, 2, . . . , n}, where n is a large positive integer greater than 1000. Let k be a positive integer less than n. Let A, B be subsets of U with |A| = |B| = k and A ∩ B = ∅. We say that a permutation of U separates A from B if one of the following is true.

- All members of A appear in the permutation before any of the members of B.

- All members of B appear in the permutation before any of the members of A.

How many permutations of U separate A from B?

Let f : A → B be an onto (or surjective) function, where A and B are nonempty sets. Define an equivalence relation ∼ on the set A as

a1 ∼ a2 if f (a1 ) = f (a2 ) ,

where a1 , a2 ∈ A. Let E = {[x] : x ∈ A} be the set of all the equivalence classes under ∼. Define a new mapping F : E → B as

F ([x]) = f (x), for all the equivalence classes [x] in E.

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

options.B: F is an onto (or surjective) function.
options.C: F is a one-to-one (or injective) function.
